judgment.regime_logic: Stage 1 calls a fragile, late-cycle-adjacent expansion with sticky above-history inflation, at low confidence (0.35) and a 20-30% recession probability. For a 7-10 year Treasury, that state cuts both ways. A recession would pull yields down and lift price through roughly 7.5 years of duration. Sticky inflation and a still-restrictive policy score (-0.22) could push yields higher, and a nominal bond has no protection against that. Exhibit 4's late-cycle tilt toward regime-adjusted methods does not carry over here. The regime_adjusted candidate (6.54%) is built from post-1990 expansion months that sit inside a secular fall in yields, and the regime label is low-confidence. Because the regime read is ambiguous, I lean on the starting yield, which does not depend on the regime call. The inflation asymmetry is the reason for trimming slightly below it rather than adding to it.
judgment.valuation_context: Valuation is the dominant lens for this asset, and it is unambiguous. The 7- and 10-year yields average 5.24%, which the yield_level signal scores +0.80, high against their own history. Over a horizon near duration, the entry yield explains most of the realised return, so yield_building_block (5.45%, including a 0.21pp variance add-back and no credit loss on Treasuries) is the anchor. The 3-year horizon is shorter than the ~7.5-year duration, so the yield path matters as well as the level: a 100bp rise over the horizon would cost about 7% of price, spread over three years. The SPF BOND10 consensus (4.00% compound) sits below today's yield. It is a 10-year average expectation and may embed some reversion or lag in the survey, so I use it as a modest counterweight for path risk rather than as a primary estimate. The historical methods (6.41%, 6.54%) are excluded. They capture 1990-2026 capital gains from falling yields, which cannot repeat from today's starting point in the same way, and they would double-count income the yield already prices.
judgment.signal_alignment: The composite (+0.18) masks a split. Valuation is strongly bullish (yield_level +0.80). Technicals are bearish: trend -0.67, relative momentum -0.56, 12-1 momentum -0.28. These do not contradict each other. The weak trailing returns (1y -3.75%, 5y -2.06%) are the yield rise that produced today's attractive entry yield. Over a multi-year horizon, bond momentum is a much weaker predictor than the starting yield. Macro alignment signals are all near zero (|score| <= 0.04), so they neither confirm nor hedge the estimate. I treat the negative technicals as a reason to sit slightly below the pure yield anchor, not as grounds for a large cut.
judgment.rationale: Final estimate: 5.26%, from 85% yield_building_block and 15% survey_consensus. This sits inside the [4.13, 6.54] range and just above the 5.19% auto-blend. The skill's guidance and Key consideration 1 make the starting yield the most defensible fixed-income building block, so it carries most of the weight. The 0.15 survey weight is a deliberate, explained haircut of about 0.2pp for two risks. First, the asymmetric inflation risk (consideration 5): sticky inflation is the stage-1 base case, and the historical sample has only one real inflation shock. Second, path risk over a 3-year horizon shorter than duration (consideration 4). Three candidates are dropped. historical_erp and regime_adjusted are biased upward by the secular fall in yields. bl_equilibrium (4.13%) is a CAPM artifact: it gives near-zero premia to assets that hedged an equity-heavy ETF market and assumes the negative stock-bond correlation that broke in 2022 (consideration 2), so I do not rely on it. Volatility stays at the covariance figure of 6.46%. Per consideration 5, that should be read as a floor in an inflationary state, and per consideration 2, backtested drawdowns understate a joint rate-and-equity shock. The estimate is held close to the yield anchor because this sleeve is 30% of the IPS benchmark (consideration 3), so an error here would shift the tracking-error budget of every candidate portfolio. Governing policy is config/ips.yaml, whose status is ratified.
